title: Valkyries instant analysis: Offense can't score in loss to Sky
text:
Valkyries shoot 27% as Golden State drops first game of season
Golden State Valkyries’ Kayla Thornton can’t reach the ball going out of bounds under pressure by Chicago Sky’s Gabriela Jaquez in the second quarter of a WNBA game at Chase Center in San Francisco, Calif.
, on Wednesday, May 13, 2025. Golden State scored at least 90 points in back-to-back games against the Storm and the Mercury, but couldn’t crack 70 on Wednesday night in a 69-62 loss to the Sky. After ending the first quarter with a nine-point lead, the Valkyries struggled to find their groove as they gave their lead early in the third period.
A flurry of buckets from Skylar Diggins and Rickea Jackson helped the Sky gain the advantage in the second half. Golden State was able to keep within a possession of the Sky up until the final minute, but one sequence of events proved to be costly. After doubling center Kamilla Cardoso in the post with just over a minute left, the Valkyries left Jackson open from the left wing.
Cardoso found Jackson spotting up and she swished a 3-pointer to give Chicago a five-point lead. On the next possession, Burton turned the ball over and the Sky hit enough free throws to close the game. Gabby Williams led the Valkyries with 18 points. Veronica Burton scored 16 points and had five turnovers.
The Valkyries had a hard time figuring out Stokes’ role in the starting lineup as the veteran is not a 3-point shooter. But against the Sky, the Valkyries seemed to have figured out how to use Stokes to open the game. Stokes finished with seven points and 11 rebounds while doing a solid job containing Cardoso. Cardoso finished with eight points on 3-of-10 shooting.
The two most consistent scorers from the Valkyries’ previous two games couldn’t buy a bucket on Wednesday night. Thornton and Salaün combined to score six points and shot 6.2% from the floor. Thornton had a plus-minus rating of -2 while Salaün was -8. The duo had 83 points across the Valkyries last two wins, but couldn’t find a way to hit perimeter shots as they were 1-for-16 as Sky defenders didn’t allow them to find an open look.
